item.title: Fiji aims to the semi-finals or even win the 2027 Rugby World Cup - Sanday
item.description: Fiji Rugby Union Chairman John Sanday says players must earn the right to wear the Flying Fijians jersey as the team aims to reach the semi-finals or even win the 2027 Rugby World Cup. Sanday highlighted this to the media saying there will be strong competition for places in the team, and players must be committed to representing Fiji rather than simply pursuing their personal ambitions.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Rugby Union Chairman John Sanday says players must earn the right to wear the Flying Fijians jersey as the team aims to reach the semi-finals or even win the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

Sanday highlighted this to the media saying there will be strong competition for places in the team, and players must be committed to representing Fiji rather than simply pursuing their personal ambitions.

He stresses that the FRU wants to establish clear standards and ensure players understand the responsibility that comes with wearing the national jersey.

When asked whether there are plans to bring players back to Fiji to reconnect with the public before the World Cup, Sanday says players are usually released about six weeks before the tournament to begin preparations.

He says this should provide enough time for the players to return home as part of their preparations.

The Flying Fijians will take on Japan in a Test match next Saturday at 5.50pm in Japan, before travelling to Europe for the Nations Championship.

item.title: Ba to celebrate historic four-title sweep with grand celebration on Oct 31st
item.description: Ba Football Association President Praneel Dayal says the grand celebration will begin around midday with a float procession making its way to Gujarati Park. The FMF IDC trophy was proudly brought home on Sunday following a 2-0 victory over Navua in the final.
item.content:encoded:
Ba Football Association President Praneel Dayal says the grand celebration will begin around midday with a float procession making its way to Gujarati Park.

The FMF IDC trophy was proudly brought home on Sunday following a 2-0 victory over Navua in the final.

He says the celebration will recognise the team's outstanding achievement of winning all four major titles in a single season.

The celebration will also provide an opportunity for players, officials and supporters to come together and mark a memorable season for Ba football.

item.title: White prioritises restoring Flying Fijians' confidence and improving game management ahead of World Cup
item.description: Restoring players' confidence, improving game management and introducing more structure without taking away Fiji's natural flair will be among the key priorities for FIJI Water Flying Fijians Head Coach Jake White as the team prepares for the 2027 Rugby World Cup. item.content:encoded:
Restoring players' confidence, improving game management and introducing more structure without taking away Fiji's natural flair will be among the key priorities for FIJI Water Flying Fijians Head Coach Jake White as the team prepares for the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

White says the Flying Fijians have lacked confidence this year despite showing their potential at the last Rugby World Cup, where they defeated Australia.

He says he wants to rebuild that confidence while ensuring the team continues to play the exciting brand of rugby Fiji is known for.

White says he will outline his plans for the 2027 Rugby World Cup when the Flying Fijians assemble in France during their November tour of Europe.

He says the discussions will focus on the team's preparations, expectations and individual areas players need to improve.

White also plans to visit players in February next year to assess their progress and ensure they are on track for the tournament in October.

The Flying Fijians will first face Japan next Saturday before travelling to Europe, where they will play France on 8 November, followed by Ireland and Italy.

item.title: Netflix secures broadcasting rights for 2030 FIFA World Cup in Spain and Andorra
item.description: Streaming platform Netflix has secured the rights to broadcast the 2030 FIFA World Cup in Spain and Andorra, marking the first time the subscription-based service will show the men's tournament. Netflix says it will broadcast all 104 matches of the world's biggest football competition live.
item.content:encoded:
Streaming platform Netflix has secured the rights to broadcast the 2030 FIFA World Cup in Spain and Andorra, marking the first time the subscription-based service will show the men's tournament.

Netflix says it will broadcast all 104 matches of the world's biggest football competition live.

The 2030 World Cup will be co-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay also hosting matches to mark the tournament's centenary.

Netflix says one match per matchday will be available to watch for free in Spain.

The company adds that all of Spain’s matches, along with the final, will also be shown on free-to-air television.

Netflix has previously broadcast live sporting events, including WWE wrestling, NFL matches and boxing.

The platform is also scheduled to broadcast the all-British heavyweight boxing contest between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua in December.

Netflix has also secured the broadcasting rights for the 2027 and 2031 editions of the FIFA Women's World Cup, w hich will be held in Brazil and the United Kingdom respectively.
